purpose: Read-only source geometry and appearance audit for local project-cover rendering. No geometry, website, source photographs, or render scripts were changed by this audit.

parameterConvention.hex: Proposed sRGB base color, not a measured reflectance value. Convert sRGB to linear before assigning numeric Blender shader colors.
parameterConvention.metallic: PBR metalness in [0,1]; coated polymer and carbon/epoxy surfaces are dielectric even if the old studio bucket used nonzero metalness.
parameterConvention.roughness: PBR roughness in [0,1], an appearance estimate to validate under neutral lighting.
parameterConvention.confidence: Photos establish visible color families and finish; none are color-chart-calibrated. Numeric shader values are proposed starting points, not photographically exact measurements.
parameterConvention.priority: Actual project photograph and current project record > matching source geometry > CAD material labels > existing studio shaders. FEA/CFD colors are data visualization, never physical pigment evidence.
parameterConvention.sourceMaterials: All five inspected models/real GLBs have no glTF materials array. mat_* mesh names are converter classifications, not authored or measured material appearances.
parameterConvention.geometryUnits: STL/GLB coordinates are retained CAD coordinates, interpreted as millimeters by the existing conversion workflow. Do not assume glTF meter conventions for these files.

criticalFindings: materialTest.glb is a two-column MTS Insight-style source model. The project's own photographs and project-data.js identify a single-column Instron 3345. Recoloring the old GLB cannot resolve this identity mismatch.

javelin.glb has mat_wood for Battery_Base due to the generic base-<instance> regex, and its four motors are in mat_aero because the Wing_Assem prefix matches the aero regex before the motor rule. Both require project-specific correction.
brakeSim.glb is exactly the single Front 2.STL rotor: one connected component, 82,888 triangles, no bracket/caliper/hat assembly merged into the steel bucket.
carbonSeat maps to models/real/seat.glb; seat maps to models/real/driverseat.glb. These are different source parts and must not be swapped.
The CFD source case really uses Javelin, but it is a simplified aero-core case without propellers. A newly lit CAD illustration is not a new CFD result.

geometry.partLevelFinding: The only file in Desktop/STL/Brake is Front 2.STL; its single connected mesh exactly equals the GLB's mat_steel geometry after canonical triangle-coordinate comparison. There is no second bracket body to separate.
geometry.otherCADLimit: Existence verified only. These other CAD parts were not opened or identified as fitted hardware. Brake Pad is not evidence of a bracket. Do not add calipers or mounts from unrelated assemblies.

references.evidence: Specifies cast iron ASTM A48 Class 40 rotors, not generic steel; 25 percent mass reduction is a design target.
Rainbow URES displacement contour, loads and constraints. Supports analyzed rotor topology, not finish or pigment. The hole pattern differs from the later dense-perforation CAD image.
Dense circular perforations and scalloped internal mount interface. Default gray is not measured cast-iron appearance.
steel is set to #bcc2c9, metalness 1, roughness 0.4 for shelf readability. This is not an independent material measurement.

mat_steel.physicalMaterial: Machined gray cast iron rotor, ASTM A48 Class 40 per project record
mat_steel.finish: Neutral silver-gray working face; subtle machining direction. Avoid chrome, rust, heat glow, rainbow temperature coloration, or invented wear marks.
mat_steel.confidence: Material identity is documented; exact as-built finish is unverified because the inspected gallery contains CAD/FEA rather than a close physical rotor photograph.

brakeSim.coverRecommendation: Render the real Front 2 rotor alone, with enough tilt to reveal its 4.75 mm thickness and keep the perforation pattern intact. Label as CAD render when needed; do not imply the FEA image and this CAD iteration are numerically identical.

geometry.notes: Actual shell source, not CF_Seat_Mold.STL. The converter preserves positions and splits normals at 40 degrees. Its notes document a non-manifold mirrored center seam: do not apply geometry smoothing/subdivision merely to improve highlights. Exact final hand-trimmed perimeter is not guaranteed by CAD.

references.evidence: Carbon/epoxy layup, demolding and trimming; shoulder/hip shell for Mk.8.
Dark woven shell with masking tape and residue; white material around the edge is temporary tape, not the composite color.
Clearly visible diagonal woven fiber pattern, directional reflection and resin sheen. Warm tint is room lighting, not bronze or gold material.
Trimmed charcoal-black composite shell; patch-dependent weave direction and broad satin/gloss highlights.
Uses a twill map with emissiveIntensity 1.1, metalness 0.3 and boosted environment intensity to remain visible on a dark shelf. Do not copy those emission/metalness settings as physical carbon/epoxy.

mat_carbon.physicalMaterial: Carbon fiber fabric in cured epoxy
mat_carbon.finish: Subtle directional woven pattern and low-amplitude bump/roughness variation; broad resin highlights. Keep the weave scale fine enough for the actual shell, not a giant checkerboard. No metallic glitter.
mat_carbon.confidence: High for dark woven composite and variable sheen. Exact weave repeat, ply directions, resin gloss and base reflectance are not calibrated by the photographs.

carbonSeat.coverRecommendation: Use the existing shell, preserve flanges and creases, show the inner support surface in a three-quarter view. A clean CAD presentation can omit tape and workshop residue without inventing upholstery or a different trim geometry.

geometry.notes: Perforated bent-sheet driver seat. Seat pan, back and lateral tabs are one source part. Harness straps are not present in this geometry. Preserve bends, mounting holes and the exact perforations.

references.evidence: Seat/harness integration and driver fit; geometry is distinct from carbonSeat.
Explicitly identifies bent-sheet aluminum; names its lone mesh mat_steel as a shared display bucket.
Pale gray/lavender CAD shading; confirms perforated folded geometry but not physical pigment.
Rainbow contour plus magenta loads and green constraints. This is analysis coloration, not a colorful painted seat.
Person seated in the car; the relevant seat-pan surface is largely occluded. Does not justify a precise brushed finish or harness color.
Light brushed aluminum display values #ccd2da, metalness 0.85, roughness 0.35.

mat_steel.physicalMaterial: Unpainted sheet aluminum, despite the generic steel bucket name
mat_steel.finish: Neutral satin sheet metal with restrained directional brushing. Do not copy lavender CAD tint or rainbow FEA coloring.
mat_steel.confidence: Aluminum identification follows the conversion documentation and existing project presentation. Alloy, exact finish and as-built surface reflectance were not established by the inspected photographs.

seat.coverRecommendation: Render the native sheet-seat model alone. Do not add guessed harness straps, cushions, black paint or carbon weave just because the project title includes harness integration.

geometry.identity: Two-column MTS Insight-style machine from a separate local downloaded model/reference package.
geometry.mismatch: The actual experiment record and the project's material-instron-frame.webp show an Instron 3345 single-column frame with silver spring-loaded grips, a black bellows face and a dark gray base. The existing model instead has two off-white columns, an off-white base, dark yoke grips, copper-colored collars and a separate pendant. These are not equivalent machines.

references.evidence: Instron 3345 (5 kN), 30 film/fabric tensile specimens and 11 bamboo bending tests; 100 mm specimen gauge length, roughly 25 mm strip widths.

Clearly labeled INSTRON 3345. Off-white single column, black bellows, dark gray textured base, silver grips/couplings, red mushroom stop on a yellow field, black controller bezel. The blue workbench and loose tools are surroundings, not machine material.
Dark charcoal coated-fabric strip marked MD-1, silver grips and caliper. Do not transfer caliper LCD color or background objects to the specimen.

Pale tan bamboo, silver/darkened metal flexure hardware, black load transducer housing. Label says 4-Point Flexure Fixture - Bottom; actual pictured configuration uses a central loading nose and two lower supports, consistent with the project's three-point test.
Despite the package name 'instron-machine', the beam reads MTS Insight and the frame has two columns. Supports the existing model's appearance only, not the equipment used in this project's tests.
Uses IMG_0378.JPG to assign 19 disconnected shells into four buckets. Classification is geometric and machine-specific; not an Instron 3345 material survey.
Off-white aero, charcoal dark, copper brass tweaks follow the old MTS reference, not the newer actual experiment photographs.

mat_aero.appliesTo: Existing MTS model ONLY: two columns plus base, merged together.

mat_dark.appliesTo: Existing MTS model ONLY: fixed beam, crosshead, two grips, pendant body. Pendant's medium gray differs from the merged dark grips.

mat_steel.appliesTo: Existing MTS model ONLY: load cylinder, base coupling, pins and pendant hardware.

mat_brass.appliesTo: Existing MTS model ONLY: two copper-toned rings inferred from its separate reference. Not evidence that the actual Instron has brass fixtures.

replacementRecommendation.preferred: Make a photo-informed reconstruction of the actual single-column Instron 3345 with a dark fabric specimen, or a tighter reconstruction of the two silver tensile grips and specimen. Use the actual photo as the construction reference. A focused grip/specimen scene reduces invented details and avoids misidentifying the old machine.
replacementRecommendation.replacementStatus: Assigned by main task to the separate material-test/build_material_test.py builder. This audit briefly produced an independent draft, then withdrew its materialTest source files when the dedicated owner was confirmed.
replacementRecommendation.geometryGuidance: Use one off-white rectangular column behind the load axis with a black ribbed bellows face; dark gray sloped-front base; silver spring-loaded jaw bodies; cylindrical couplings; dark load-transducer body; red emergency stop with yellow surround. Do not copy two columns, a cream base, black square yoke grips or the MTS pendant. Use the documented 100 mm gauge span and approximately 25 mm strip width only for the test coupon; machine dimensions are unmeasured.
replacementRecommendation.precisionLimit: These colors and roughness values are proposed neutral-light starting points based on uncalibrated photographs. Geometry is a visual reconstruction, not manufacturer CAD or a dimensionally certified digital twin. No toolbox colors, colored charts or FEA palettes may be treated as physical material.

geometry.identity: Actual local Javelin airframe assembly export; source STL set does not include separately named propeller files.
currentBucketingErrors: Battery_Base-1 matches generic base-\d before any battery rule, becoming mat_wood. No evidence supports a wood battery tray.
Four T Motor F90 STL basenames include Wing_Assem, so nosecone|tailcone|wing|naca wins before the later motor regex. The motors are in mat_aero, not mat_dark.
Battery_Retainer-1 is in mat_dark due to 'battery'. It is a structural retainer, not proof of black battery casing material.
The studio's javelin matTweak includes printed, but the actual GLB has no mat_printed mesh. It does not fix mat_wood.

references.evidence: PPA-CF chassis, ASA antenna fairings, PC-FR parts, bonded carbon tube spars. Do not substitute a woven carbon laminate appearance over all printed skin.

Identifies printed polymer families and candidate APC prop sizes. The overview says KV1300 while the vendor CAD filename says 1500kV; appearance audit does not certify motor electrical identity or change website specs.
Four black two-blade props, dark printed body/wing surfaces, black-and-silver motors with visible copper windings, silver prop nuts. Actual photo agrees with the relevant website visual references.
Charcoal body, evident print/finishing lines, patchy satin reflection; black props, silver motor edges and pitot tube.
Black motor bell with exposed silver rim/spokes and orange-copper winding highlights; black two-blade propeller and bright silver nut. Do not make the whole motor gray plastic.
Dark printed/fairing surface, black lens and vent interiors, silver pitot with dark tip. Gold marking is a decal, not a gold airframe material.
Aero #3a3e44 and dark #24272c support a dark presentation but inherit generic material/mesh classification mistakes.

mat_aero.physicalMaterial: Dark printed airframe polymers; exact per-part polymer family is not fully resolved by the photographs.
mat_aero.mandatoryException: Remove the four motor parts from this assignment before rendering. Use per-STL isolation below; the current merged bucket cannot give airframe and motors distinct finish.

mat_wood.physicalMaterial: Battery support/tray, likely printed polymer, not wood
mat_wood.confidence: Correction away from wood is supported by source naming and project material descriptions. Precise tray pigment is not visible in the inspected assembled photos; dark neutral polymer is a conservative interior approximation.

mat_dark.physicalMaterial: Mixed small electronics housings and battery retainer
mat_dark.confidence: Broad default only. Visible optical glass and metal fittings deserve separate shaders if isolated; cannot infer every electronic component's finish from this merged mesh.

mat_steel.mandatoryException: Photo shows a dark tip. If the tube mesh includes that tip, isolate it geometrically and apply dielectric #242629; do not paint the entire tube black.

partLevelSources.motorIsolationLimit: The inspected motor instance -2 has 7,102 faces and ONE connected shell, approximately 34.7 x 33.4 x 33.4 mm. Splitting connected components will not recover separate silver, black and copper surfaces. Use the vendor STEP topology or intentional face-level masks reviewed against the photo. STEP includes gray/white/red COLOUR_RGB values, but those CAD colors do not override the actual black/silver/copper photo.

motor_black_finish.note: Black anodized-looking motor exterior; underlying finish chemistry is not proven by photo.

motor_copper_winding.note: Use only on actual or explicitly reconstructed winding geometry visible through the motor openings, never arbitrary orange rings.

propeller.note: Four dark two-blade props are visible in the real build. Exact blade sections/pitch are not recovered from photos; any added prop mesh must be described as a visual reconstruction, not the certified APC blade geometry.

javelin.coverRecommendation: Keep original airframe geometry and dark polymer texture; isolate motors by their original STL names before assigning materials. Add photo-informed propellers only if needed for the as-built presentation. Do not invent woven carbon skin, blue bodywork, glowing motors or unsupported material distinctions.

coverSource.addedGeometry: Four 132.08 mm nominal diameter, two-blade display propellers, annular hubs and silver prop nuts. Chord, twist, handedness and blade profiles are illustrative approximations informed by photos and the 5.2-inch candidate size, not original APC CAD or flight-ready geometry.
coverSource.materialLimit: Motor face masks expose shaft/front lip in silver and retain black bell; they are appearance approximations on the exact supplied motor mesh. Copper windings are absent from that simplified source and were not fabricated.
coverSource.searchLimit: No separate or identifiable embedded prop filename was found. Binary assembly string scanning does not prove that every proprietary CAD configuration is absent; no complete source export with blades was discovered in these supplied folders.

ansysCfd.sourceGLBRole: Available geometry of the real analysis object, suitable for an explicitly illustrative CAD cover; not byte-identical to the solver's simplified aero-core geometry.
ansysCfd.preferredExactAnalysisSourceStatus: Documented in the local CFD case study. The reference scripts point to C:/Users/oc/Desktop/Codex_Ansys, which does not exist at audit time. Exact STEP and solved case/data were not located in the inspected CFD package or Javelin/STL directories; do not claim they were loaded.

references.evidence: Explicitly identifies the completed Javelin VTOL cruise validation case at 300 kph / Mach 0.245, with estimated references limiting coefficient claims to process validation.

Flow case identifies Javelin_V1, an aero-core 8-solid-body subset from the full 54-body model, propellers ignored, alpha 3 degrees. Continuation names the fused validation STEP and its conforming-mesh workflow.
Names the saved conforming_alpha3 case/data workflow and external aircraft wall selection. It is evidence of the documented workflow, not proof the local solved files are currently available.
Actual saved presentation shows Cp on Javelin's aerodynamic shape with a labeled numerical legend. Yellow/green/red/blue are pressure-coefficient values, not the body finish.

mat_aero.appliesTo: Javelin's physical printed airframe, for a neutral-lit geometry illustration only. Exclude motor pieces from this bucket.

mat_wood.appliesTo: Battery support only if the full illustrative model is shown; omit for an aero-core-inspired illustration.

mat_dark.appliesTo: Electronics only if showing the full illustrative assembly; omit from aero-core-inspired view.

mat_steel.appliesTo: Pitot only if part of the displayed illustrative assembly; exact solver inclusion was not verified.

ansysCfd.coverRecommendation: Use a distinct top/three-quarter view of the real Javelin analysis object. Prefer the original airframe STLs listed under javelin.partLevelSources.printedAirframe when making an aero-core-inspired illustration; do not claim that this seven-file assembly reconstructs the documented eight-solid solver subset exactly. Omit newly modeled propellers from a depiction of the analysis setup. Pairing a real saved CFD result image with the geometric render is acceptable if the result remains identifiable as that original image.
nonFabricationRules: No invented streamline paths, velocity vectors, pressure bands, Mach fields, Cp scales, force numbers or colorful mesh plots on newly rendered geometry.
If adding computational-looking geometry edges, label them as a geometry illustration; they are not a Fluent mesh or converged flow solution.

A real data overlay requires the matching solved surface data, correct geometry correspondence, original units and legend. Existing saved plots may be retained with their provenance; do not synthesize a new field by recoloring the body.
Keep process-validation limitations for estimated area, length and moment center. An attractive cover does not upgrade numerical credibility or prove flight performance.
ansysCfd.currentCoverDecision: Main task has built a presentation monitor textured with the unchanged genuine Cp plot. No new CFD geometry or fields are needed from this audit.

verification.photoInspectionMethod: view_image on actual local image files; sources marked viewed above.
verification.sourcePreservation: All five original GLB SHA-256 values rechecked unchanged after cover-source construction.

followUpDraftReview.javelin: Draft is too light/smooth and lacks all four propellers. Darken airframe to #242629, metalness 0, roughness 0.58; use the cover-only source with isolated black/silver motors and dark polymer battery tray. Original photos show print/finishing marks, not a polished gray aircraft.
followUpDraftReview.carbonSeat: Draft has an over-wide bright reflection and conspicuous checker pattern. Keep dielectric carbon/epoxy, metalness 0, roughness about 0.5, clearcoat about 0.12; reduce checker contrast and retain fine directional weave. These are neutral-light visual recommendations, not measured resin values.
followUpDraftReview.seat: Draft silhouette and silver family are reasonable; neutral #C8CCD0, metallic 1, roughness 0.4. Avoid making it white plastic or mirror chrome.
followUpDraftReview.brakeSim: Draft is too bright/chrome-like for the conservative cast-iron interpretation. #A3A5A8, metallic 1, roughness 0.48. Geometry is the real dense-perforated rotor; keep its thickness/holes.
followUpDraftReview.materialTest: Reject the draft as the project apparatus: it depicts the different two-column MTS machine. Main task delegated the real Instron 3345 photo reconstruction to material-test/build_material_test.py; this audit no longer owns that geometry.
